title: Hávamál Selections
subtitle: Sayings of the High One
description: Ancient Norse wisdom poems attributed to Odin, offering guidance on survival, knowledge, and the values of the Viking age.

quotes.textLatin: Within the gates ere a man shall go, (Full warily let him watch,) Full long let him look about him; For little he knows where a foe may lurk, And sit in the seats within.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:

https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#lg1.2.1

quotes.textLatin: Hail to the giver! a guest has come; Where shall the stranger sit? Swift shall he be who with swords shall try The proof of his might to make.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 2 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#lg1.2.2

quotes.textLatin: Fire he needs who with frozen knees Has come from the cold without; Food and clothes must the farer have, The man from the mountains come.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:

https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: Water and towels and welcoming speech Should he find who comes to the feast; If renown he would get, and again be greeted, Wisely and well must he act.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 4 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: Wits must he have who wanders wide, But all is easy at home; At the witless man the wise shall wink When among such men he sits.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 5 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: A man shall not boast of his keenness of mind, But keep it close in his breast; To the silent and wise does ill come seldom When he goes as guest to a house; (For a faster friend one never finds Than wisdom tried and true.)
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 6 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#lg1.2.6

quotes.textLatin: The knowing guest who goes to the feast, In silent attention sits; With his ears he hears, with his eyes he watches, Thus wary are wise men all.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 7 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: Happy the one who wins for himself Favor and praises fair; Less safe by far is the wisdom found That is hid in another’s heart.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 8 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: Happy the man who has while he lives Wisdom and praise as well, For evil counsel a man full oft Has from another’s heart.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 9 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: A better burden may no man bear For wanderings wide than wisdom; It is better than wealth on unknown ways, And in grief a refuge it gives.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 10 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: The son of a king shall be silent and wise, And bold in battle as well; Bravely and gladly a man shall go, Till the day of his death is come.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 15 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: The sluggard believes he shall live forever, If the fight he faces not; But age shall not grant him the gift of peace, Though spears may spare his life.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 16 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: He alone is aware who has wandered wide, And far abroad has fared, How great a mind is guided by him That wealth of wisdom has.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 18 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: Shun not the mead, but drink in measure; Speak to the point or be still; For rudeness none shall rightly blame thee If soon thy bed thou seekest.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 19 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: A paltry man and poor of mind At all things ever mocks; For never he knows, what he ought to know, That he is not free from faults.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 22 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: The witless man is awake all night, Thinking of many things; Care-worn he is when the morning comes, And his woe is just as it was.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 23 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: A witless man, when he meets with men, Had best in silence abide; For no one shall find that nothing he knows, If his mouth is not open too much. (But a man knows not, if nothing he knows, When his mouth has been open too much.)
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 27 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#lg1.2.27

quotes.textLatin: Wise shall he seem who well can question, And also answer well; Nought is concealed that men may say Among the sons of men.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 28 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: Often he speaks who never is still With words that win no faith; The babbling tongue, if a bridle it find not, Oft for itself sings ill.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 29 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: Crooked and far is the road to a foe, Though his house on the highway be; But wide and straight is the way to a friend, Though far away he fare.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 34 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: Forth shall one go, nor stay as a guest In a single spot forever; Love becomes loathing if long one sits By the hearth in another’s home.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 35 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: Better a house, though a hut it be, A man is master at home; A pair of goats and a patched-up roof Are better far than begging.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 36 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#lg1.2.36

quotes.textLatin: Away from his arms in the open field A man should fare not a foot; For never he knows when the need for a spear Shall arise on the distant road.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 38 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: Friends shall gladden each other with arms and garments, As each for himself can see; Gift-givers’ friendships are longest found, If fair their fates may be.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 41 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#lg1.2.41

quotes.textLatin: To his friend a man a friend shall prove, And gifts with gifts requite; But men shall mocking with mockery answer, And fraud with falsehood meet.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 42 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: To his friend a man a friend shall prove, To him and the friend of his friend; But never a man shall friendship make With one of his foeman’s friends.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 43 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: If a friend thou hast whom thou fully wilt trust, And good from him wouldst get, Thy thoughts with his mingle, and gifts shalt thou make, And fare to find him oft.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 44 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: Young was I once, and wandered alone, And nought of the road I knew; Rich did I feel when a comrade I found, For man is man’s delight.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 47 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: On the hillside drear the fir-tree dies, All bootless its needles and bark; It is like a man whom no one loves,— Why should his life be long?
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 50 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: No great thing needs a man to give, Oft little will purchase praise; With half a loaf and a half-filled cup A friend full fast I made.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 52 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#ch1.2

quotes.textLatin: Among Fitjung’s sons saw I well-stocked folds,— Now bear they the beggar’s staff; Wealth is as swift as a winking eye, Of friends the falsest it is.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 76 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription
https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#lg1.2.76

quotes.textLatin: Cattle die, and kinsmen die, And so one dies one’s self; But a noble name will never die, If good renown one gets.
quotes.author: Hávamál
quotes.source:
The Poetic Edda · Henry Adams Bellows, 1923 · Hávamál, stanza 77 · Public-domain text; Project Gutenberg transcription

quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.source:

quotes.source:

quotes.source:

quotes.source:

quotes.author: Völuspá
quotes.source:

https://www.gutenberg.org/files/73533/73533-h/73533-h.htm#lg1.1.6

quotes.source:

quotes.author: Völuspá

quotes.source:
